title: Replicator Dynamics of Co-Evolving Networks
publisher: arXiv (AAAI-format workshop paper; Galstyan, Kianercy, Allahverdyan, USC ISI)

key_points.claim: Proposes a model of network co-evolution in which agents play repeated games with neighbors and adapt both behaviors and links via reinforcement learning. Relevant to the social-structure/interaction-topology and learning aspects of artificial societies.
key_points.evidence_quote: agents that play repeated games with their neighbors, and adapt their behaviors network links based on the outcome of those games. The adaptation is achieved through a simple reinforcement learning scheme.

key_points.claim: Argues that modeling individual and network dynamics separately is too limited. Attributes and topology should be coupled, as in homophily and opinion dynamics.
key_points.evidence_quote: modeling individual and network dynamics separately is too limited to capture realistic behavior of networks

key_points.claim: Agents use stateless Q-learning with Boltzmann exploration. In the continuous-time limit the collective dynamics become coupled replicator equations. The temperature T sets the exploration/exploitation tradeoff and adds an entropic term.
key_points.evidence_quote: Here the inverse temperature =1/T>0 controls exploration/exploitation tradeoff

key_points.claim: Factorizing strategies into a partner-choice probability c_xy and an action probability p_x^i gives coupled equations for strategy and network-link evolution. The authors note that this assumption may destroy some Nash equilibria.
key_points.evidence_quote: c_{xy} is the probability that the agent x will initiate a game with the agent y, whereas p_x^i is the probability that he will choose action i

key_points.claim: In a 3-agent coordination game, the symmetric interior rest point (all link weights 1/2) becomes stable when 4T>1. Pure Nash configurations also exist, such as two agents pairing up while the third is isolated.
key_points.evidence_quote: for 4T>1 all three eigenvalues of this Jacobian become negative, thus making the interior rest point stable

key_points.claim: In a Rock-Paper-Scissors example, the stability of the symmetric link configuration depends on the payoff parameter epsilon and on T. At T=0 with negative average reward, agents avoid playing each other.
key_points.evidence_quote: the interior rest point becomes stable whenever $T>\epsilon/12$ for $1>\epsilon>0$ , and $T>|\epsilon|/6$ for $-1<\epsilon<0$

key_points.claim: The background section reviews related network models. These are Erdős–Rényi random graphs, Barabási–Albert preferential attachment (p_k ~ k^-3), the Holme–Newman co-evolving opinion model with a phase transition, Skyrms–Pemantle adaptive networks, and network-formation games.
key_points.evidence_quote: while varying the parameter $\phi$ , the model undergoes a phase transition from a phase in which opinions are diverse to one in which most individuals hold the same opinion

key_points.claim: Limitations: the analysis covers only 3 agents and simple games. Full analysis and larger systems are left to future work.
key_points.evidence_quote: we intend to go beyond the three-agent systems considered here and examine larger systems

reliability_notes: Full text was fetched. It is a short, preliminary, theory-oriented arXiv paper with no empirical validation or large-scale agent-based simulation. It is useful for co-evolving networks and learning agents, not for full artificial societies. The AAAI copyright line says 2018, which looks like a template artifact.
